Remaining hand is cheap and useful; keeping it and drawing back up to 6.

Play Rocket Boots for +1 HP and a Tech upgrade (raises Iron Man hand size). Pay with Genius.

Clocks: T 0/3, alter-ego end would add ~3 threat (1 per-round + Ultron SCH 1 + Drone SCH 1) and hit the threshold. Hero form keeps threat to +1 per round. HP 10. Change to Iron Man.

Pay Punch with Repulsor Blast + Mark V Helmet, keeping Genius (2 resources) to pay for Arc Reactor, which readies Iron Man for a second basic attack this turn.
Play Arc Reactor with Genius, then exhaust it to ready Iron Man for a basic attack on the Drone.
Basic attack the 1-HP Drone to clear the minion before the villain phase. Then exhaust Arc Reactor to ready Iron Man for one more attack on Ultron.
Exhaust Arc Reactor to ready Iron Man, then basic attack Ultron for 1 more damage.
Basic attack Ultron for 1 (13 to 12). Clocks: T 0/3, hero threat +1, HP 10; no minions now, so the villain phase is light.
HP 10 vs base ATK 2 + boost (max ~4). Not defending keeps Iron Man ready for my next turn's attack.
T is 1 of 3. Placing threat would bring it to 2, and the next villain phase would push it to the threshold. A Drone is 1 HP and dies to one basic attack, so take the Drone.
HP 7 vs Drone ATK 1 + boost (max ~3). Not lethal; keep Iron Man ready to attack next turn.
Clocks: T 1/3 (+1 per round, +2 planning = 4 would advance the scheme); HP 6 vs incoming up to 6 (Ultron 2 + boost + Drone 1 + Adv Drone 1). Basic thwart removes 2 threat, taking T to 0.
Exhaust Arc Reactor to ready Iron Man so he can attack the 1-HP Drone this turn and still defend in the villain phase.
Kill the 1-HP Drone to cut incoming damage in the villain phase (HP 6). Iron Man exhausting means he won't defend, but defending would only save 1 and cost next turn's power.
Clocks: T 0/3, hero threat +1; HP 6 vs Ultron 2 + boost + Adv Drone 1 + boost. Nothing else is payable without spending War Machine; end turn with Iron Man ready at the end of the phase.
Keep hand: War Machine and Pepper Potts are useful next turn, and Energy is needed for payment.

HP 6 vs Ultron 2 + boost plus Adv Drone 1 next: without defending, I could drop to 1-3 HP. Defending saves 1 (DEF 1). Iron Man stays exhausted only until Arc Reactor readies him next turn, so the cost is small.
Avoid adding another Drone minion (extra attacker against HP 6). I have no energy in pool to spend, so the effect should cost me nothing.
Discard the Energy card rather than War Machine (my ally). Energy is the least valuable card in hand.
T would go 1 to 2; next turn I can ready Iron Man with Arc Reactor and thwart 2. Adding a Drone would add an attacker against HP 5, which is the tighter clock.

Mockingbird is a 3-cost ally with 3 HP that adds board presence and a potential attack or thwart. Relentless Assault needs energy I don't have in hand.
Keep all cards: Pepper Potts, War Machine and Mockingbird are all useful next turn. Draw up to 6.

Clocks: scheme at 1/10 with about 4 threat per round in alter-ego. Two threat now costs less than a Drone that adds 1 threat every villain phase for the rest of the game. Also keeps the board smaller.

Spend a physical resource (paying by discarding a hand card) rather than adding a Drone: a new Drone adds 1 SCH every villain phase and another attacker while I'm at 4 HP. I'll see the payment options first and pick the least valuable card.
Pay with Pepper Potts, the least valuable card in hand. Keep Uppercut (5 damage), Mockingbird and War Machine.

Play Mockingbird: its response stuns Ultron, so Ultron's attack does nothing in the villain phase. Then recover, switch to Iron Man, ready him with Arc Reactor, and thwart to pull T below the danger line.

Stun Ultron so its attack this villain phase does nothing (only removes the stun). Ultron is the bigger attacker; the Drones are 1 ATK each.
Stun Ultron: it is the biggest attacker (ATK 2 + boost). I must end the turn as Iron Man so the stun cancels its attack.

HP 5 vs Advanced Drone 1 + boost (max ~3): not lethal. Not defending keeps Iron Man ready for next turn's thwart and attack.
HP 4. Not defending risks 1 HP on a +2 boost. Iron Man defends (DEF 1), so damage is only the boost; Arc Reactor can ready him next turn. Mockingbird at 2 HP would die to any boost.

Clocks: T 5/10 (scheme adds ~3/round). HP 4 vs incoming ~6 with three minions/Ultron attacking as hero: lethal. Exhaust Arc Reactor to ready Iron Man so he can kill a 1-HP Drone this turn; plain Drones don't replace themselves when defeated.
Kill Drone#12 (1 HP) with Iron Man, cutting the attackers to Ultron, Adv Drone and Drone#6. Keep Mockingbird ready to absorb Ultron's attack. Thwarting would leave 4 attackers against my 4 HP.

Clocks: T 5/10. HP 4 vs Ultron 2+boost, Adv Drone 1+boost, Drone#6 1. Mockingbird attacks Drone#6 (1 HP): kill it, so fewer attackers. Mockingbird takes 1 (2 to 1 HP) but readies at end of turn to block in the villain phase.

Clocks: T 5/10, alter-ego end would add ~11 threat (lose). Stay hero. HP 4 vs Ultron 2+boost, Adv Drone 1+boost, Drone#6 1. Iron Man and Mockingbird both ready at end of turn for defense. Only option left is to end turn.
Keep hand: War Machine, Stark Tower and Uppercut are all useful next turn. Hand size 3 is fine.
T 6/10. Taking 2 threat (to 8) avoids another attacker against my 4 HP. Next turn I can thwart with Iron Man (2), Mockingbird (1) and War Machine if needed.

Mockingbird is at 1 HP and would die to its own consequential damage on its next attack, so it is expendable. Defending with it keeps my HP at 4 (Iron Man defending would drop me to 1-3), and Iron Man stays ready for next turn's thwart.
T 8 to 9. A new Drone would be an extra attacker every round against my 4 HP; threat is the cheaper cost, and I have Iron Man thwart (2) and War Machine (thwart 1) to pull it back next turn.
HP 4. Unblocked worst case: Adv Drone 1+2 boost plus Drone#6 1 = 4, which is lethal. Iron Man's DEF 1 cuts it to 3 max, leaving me at 1+. Arc Reactor can ready him next turn.

Clocks: T 9/10, one more threat advances to Countdown (no threat removal). Must thwart. Ready Iron Man with Arc Reactor, then basic thwart 2 (T 9 to 7). Iron Man readies again at end of turn to defend.
Basic thwart removes 2 threat (T 9 to 7), keeping the scheme away from the threshold.
Clocks: T 7/10. Alter-ego end adds ~4-6 (loss). Stay hero. HP 3 vs incoming up to ~6 minus DEF 1 if Iron Man defends. Nothing else is affordable without spending War Machine and Uppercut. End turn.
Keep hand; nothing to gain from discarding.

Placing 2 threat takes T 8 to 10, advancing to Countdown to Oblivion (no threat removal) and also bringing in a Drone. A Drone now keeps T at 8 without the advance. Same attacker count, and the scheme stays removable.

Defending Ultron with Iron Man or taking its hit gives the same total damage once the Drone's 1 is counted (Iron Man can only defend once). Taking Ultron's hit lets me see the boost first and decide on Iron Man for the Drone attack.

choices.reasoning: Duplicate Powered Gauntlets is the weakest card; Strength is the only resource source, so keep it. Replace one duplicate for a fresh draw.
Keep the hand: Strength for resources, Tac Team and Gauntlet to build, Combat Training for ATK. Further mulligans would cost more than they gain.

Draw first: Futurist (once per round, free) to find a card before choosing what to play. Clocks: T 0/3, alter-ego threat about 5 next villain phase, HP 9 vs drone 1 + Ultron 2, so I need to thwart or build now.
Genius gives 2 mental resources, enough to pay for a 2-3 cost card this turn alongside Strength. Emergency is only a 1-threat reduction.
Play Tac Team (support, usable in alter-ego) to start 2 damage per turn. Pay with Strength and Repulsor Blast, keeping Genius and Gauntlets for Uppercut.
Pay Tac Team with Powered Gauntlets (energy) and Strength (2 physical). This keeps Repulsor Blast and Genius to pay for Uppercut after I change to hero, and keeps Combat Training.
Use Tac Team now for 2 damage. Target will be Ultron, which is the main HP pool. The Drone can be handled by my hero attack after I change form.
Hit Ultron for 2. The 1-HP Drone is a waste for 2 damage; my hero basic attack can kill it after the form change.
Change to hero form so I can use Uppercut (a Hero Action attack) and my hero's basic attack. Ending as hero is correct: alter-ego threat would take T past 3 with Ultron's SCH added.
Uppercut deals 5 to Ultron (15 to 10). Paying 3 with Repulsor Blast and Genius is the best use of the cards left. Combat Training stays in hand and fits my hero hand size of 1.
Pay with Repulsor Blast and Genius; keep Combat Training as a permanent ATK upgrade for later.
Basic attack the 1-HP Drone to remove an engaged minion (1 ATK, 1 SCH) before the villain phase. Iron Man readies at end of turn, so there's no defensive cost.
Hand size is 1 in hero form and I hold only Combat Training, so no discard is needed. Draw up to 1.
Do not defend: 9 HP easily absorbs Ultron's 2 ATK plus boost, and defending would exhaust Iron Man and lose next turn's basic power.
Scheme is at 1/3 and the per-round threat would reach the threshold within two rounds if I add threat now. A 1-HP Drone is easy to clear with my basic attack, so put a Drone into play.
Take 1 damage from the 1-ATK Drone; defending would exhaust Iron Man through my next turn.
Scheme in danger (T 1/3, hero threat about 3). Basic thwart removes 2 from The Crimson Cowl, bringing it to 0. Iron Man readies at end of turn and can still defend.
Use Tac Team on the Drone, not Ultron. HP is 5 against about 5 incoming, so removing the 1-ATK minion before the villain phase matters more than 2 damage to a 10-HP villain.
Kill the Drone (1 ATK, 1 SCH) before the villain phase to cut incoming damage and threat.
Stay hero: alter-ego threat (1 per round + Ultron SCH 1 + boost) could reach the threshold of 3. End turn; Iron Man readies and can defend in the villain phase.
Keep Combat Training, since my hero hand size is 1 and I can't pay for it anyway. Draw up to 1.
HP 5 vs Ultron 2 + boost (up to 3 would be lethal unblocked). Defending with Iron Man reduces damage by DEF 1. Survival outweighs next turn's basic power.
At 4 HP, another Drone would add a 1-ATK attacker each villain phase. Taking the threat (1 to 2 of 3) keeps my attacker count down, and Iron Man's thwart (2) can clear it back to 0 next turn.

Hero form means Ultron's 2 ATK plus a Drone hit with no defender, which is lethal at 2 HP. Alter-ego form makes the villain scheme instead: no damage to me this phase. The scheme advances to Stage 2, which does not lose the game. Change to Tony Stark (Futurist and REC are then available).
Futurist is free once per round and draws a card before I spend resources. I need a heal, a defence, or a way to cut threat.
First Aid heals 2 on Tony or Iron Man, which matters at 2 HP. I need a heal more than Chase Them Down's conditional threat removal.

Clock check: HP 2 and the villain phase adds threat (about 4), so the scheme advances this round regardless. HP is the urgent clock. First Aid heals 2 on Tony Stark (2 to 4 HP), paying with Combat Training.
Use last Tac Team counter on the Drone (1 HP) to remove its SCH from the alter-ego scheme step. Ultron is at 10 HP and not close to dying, so the scheme is the priority.
Kill the Drone (1 SCH) to reduce alter-ego threat this villain phase.

Clocks: T 0/5, alter-ego threat next villain phase ≈ 1+2+1+2+boost ≥ 6, which would lose, so I must end as hero. HP 4 vs incoming ≈ Ultron 2 + two Drones 2 + boost ≈ 4-6. Futurist is free and draws before I spend anything.
Tac Team is the best card to keep: it's repeatable 2-damage and I can keep one card as hero (hand size 1). Nick Fury is a one-shot.

Clocks: T 0/5 (Countdown, threat cannot be removed, +1/round as hero). HP 4 is the urgent clock; alter-ego threat would lose (1+2+1+1+boost ≥ 5), so I must end as hero. Recover (alter-ego only) heals 3 now, before I change form. Iron Man will ready at end of turn for defence.
Change to Iron Man (hero form). Alter-ego threat would add about 4 to an uncancellable Countdown scheme (threshold 5). Hero form needed for the basic attack on a Drone.
Relentless Assault on Drone#27 (1 HP). Paying with physical (Combat Training) gives overkill: the excess 4 damage goes to Ultron. This clears a Drone and puts 4 on Ultron.

Pay with The Power of Aggression (2 wild). Wild counts as physical, so overkill still applies and the 4 excess goes to Ultron. Hero hand size is 1, so the other cards in hand are going to be used or discarded anyway.
Play Hulk (ally, 5 HP, 3 ATK). He can attack Ultron now and later defend. Pay with Combat Training and War Machine, which I can't otherwise use this turn and would discard at end of turn anyway.
Pay Hulk with War Machine (wild) and Combat Training (physical). Keeps Haymaker and Tac Team for next turn, but my hero hand is 1 anyway.
Hulk attacks Ultron for 3 (6 to 3). He readies at end of turn and can defend. Puts Ultron in range of Haymaker or Tac Team next turn, which is the faster way to end the 17-HP stage.

Hulk's trigger deals 2 to an enemy. Ultron at 3 HP drops to 1, so next turn Iron Man's free basic attack finishes it and my cards stay free for the Drone. Damage on Ultron is permanent progress; the Drone is only 1 ATK.
Discard Tac Team (3 cost) and keep Haymaker (2 cost, 3 damage) to finish Ultron at 1 HP next turn.
Keep Haymaker and draw up to hand size 1.
No defender: 7 HP absorbs Ultron's 2 + boost (worst case about 4). Hulk at 3 HP would die to a boost, and defending with Iron Man would cost his basic attack, which can finish Ultron at 1 HP.

Countdown to Oblivion cannot have threat removed and loses at 5. Placing threat (1 to 2) would bring it close to the threshold. A Drone adds only 1 ATK per villain phase, which Hulk can defend against.

No defender: the Drone's 1 ATK costs me 1 HP (3 to 2). Defending with Iron Man would keep him exhausted through my next turn, which costs his free basic attack. Next turn Hulk can finish Ultron (1 HP) and Iron Man's basic attack can clear the Drone.
Defend with Iron Man: DEF 1 reduces the 1-ATK Drone to 0, so I stay at 2 HP. Losing next turn's 1-damage basic attack is cheaper than losing 1 HP at 2 HP, and Hulk stays ready for a 3-damage attack.

Taking 3 damage at 2 HP would defeat me. Placing 2 threat on the side scheme Under Attack is the only option that keeps me alive. Its crisis stops threat removal from the main scheme, which is a real cost, but the main scheme only loses at 5 and it is at 1.

Scheme at 4/5 with per-round +1 in the villain phase (lethal at threshold 5), and crisis stops thwarting it; no card in hand can change that. If the engine resolves differently, killing a Drone (1 ATK) is better than killing Ultron, because Ultron's stage-2 form at full HP gets +1 ATK per Drone engaged. Hulk's trigger may let me pick a target.
Hulk's trigger: deal 2 to Ultron (1 HP), defeating stage 1. It's the only damage that advances toward winning, and the Drones are only 1 ATK each.
No legal action reduces threat on Countdown to Oblivion (crisis blocks thwarts), and Haymaker can't be paid for. Ending the turn is the only remaining option.
Keep Haymaker and draw to hand size 1; nothing else to do.
